key_findings.claim: Existing MWP solvers rely on shallow heuristics to achieve high performance on benchmark datasets.
key_findings.evidence: MWP solvers that do not have access to the question asked in the MWP can still solve a large fraction of MWPs. Similarly, models that treat MWPs as bag-of-words can also achieve surprisingly high accuracy. The best performing model achieved a 5-fold cross-validation accuracy of 64.4% on ASDiv-A and 77.7% on MAWPS when questions were removed. A constrained model without word-order information achieved 51.2% on ASDiv-A and 77.9% on MAWPS.
key_findings.limitations: We do not claim that every model trained on these datasets relies on the occurrence of specific words in the input problem for prediction the way our constrained model does.

key_findings.claim: Existing benchmark English MWP datasets (MAWPS and ASDiv-A) suffer from artifacts, making them unreliable to gauge the performance of MWP solvers.
key_findings.evidence: The majority of problems in the existing datasets can be solved by simple heuristics even without word-order information or the question text. SOTA models exploit these artifacts, and the bulk of their success is due to 'Easy' problems (those solved without the question).

key_findings.claim: The paper introduces a challenge dataset, SVAMP (Simple Variations on Arithmetic Math word Problems), for more robust evaluation of methods developed to solve elementary level math word problems.
key_findings.evidence: SVAMP was created by applying carefully chosen variations (Question Sensitivity, Reasoning Ability, and Structural Invariance) over examples sampled from existing datasets (ASDiv-A). It consists of a final set of 1000 one-unknown arithmetic word problems with grade level up to 4.

key_findings.claim: State-of-the-art (SOTA) models achieve substantially lower accuracy on SVAMP, demonstrating that much remains to be done even for the simplest of MWPs and that existing models cannot robustly solve elementary level word problems.
key_findings.evidence: The best accuracy achieved by SOTA models is 43.8% on SVAMP. This failure of SOTA models on SVAMP points to the extent to which they rely on simple heuristics in training data to make their prediction.

key_findings.claim: Problems in SVAMP are more challenging for models and are less vulnerable to being solved by simple patterns, requiring contextual information.
key_findings.evidence: The accuracy of models drops by half when questions are removed from SVAMP examples compared to ASDiv-A. The constrained model (without word-order information) achieves only 18.3% accuracy on SVAMP, which is marginally better than the majority template baseline. Both the Question Sensitivity and Structural Invariance categories of variations show an increase in accuracy when their examples are removed, indicating they make SVAMP more challenging.

key_findings.claim: The capability of existing models to solve simple one-unknown arithmetic word problems is overestimated.
key_findings.evidence: This paper gives a negative answer to the question of whether existing NLP models are able to solve elementary math word problems, based on empirical evidence from benchmark datasets and performance on the proposed challenge dataset SVAMP.

key_findings.claim: Current methods are incapable of properly associating numbers to their context, especially in problems with more than two numbers.
key_findings.evidence: While the model can solve many problems consisting of only two numbers in the input text (even in our challenge set), it performs very badly on problems having more than two numbers.
